keyFindings.description: `ignoreMutation: () => true` on a leaf node view also swallows ProseMirror's synthetic selection record (prosemirror-view 1.42.3 dist/index.js:4773-4791, consulted through CustomNodeViewDesc.ignoreMutation at :1632-1634). The leaf default, `!contentDOM && mutation.type != "selection"` (:1110-1111), already ignores the → swap the comment cites, so the override buys nothing and leaves `state.selection` stale when a DOM selection settles inside the fallback link (drag-selecting its words, or a click in a browser that keeps focus on the editing host); the next keymap command then edits at the old caret. Fix: drop the property (or `(m) => m.type !== "selection"`) and update picture-view.test.ts:84.

`stopEvent` is true for every event inside the fallback , so `dragstart` whose source is that anchor (an `a[href]` is draggable by default, and the browser picks the nearest draggable ancestor-or-self of the mousedown target) never reaches `handlers.dragstart` (index.js:3802-3832 via eventBelongsToView :3173-3183); `view.dragging` stays null, and on drop `handleDrop` (:3849-3903) parses the browser's own `text/html` for the link and inserts `[KEY notes-md](http://…/issues/KEY/artifacts/notes-md?v=1)` at the drop point while the picture node stays - words the view invented reach the stored markdown, and the original is not moved. No `handleDrop`/`transformPasted` prop intercepts (grep of packages/dispatch/web/src and packages/proof-editor/src). Fix: `link.draggable = false` so the wrapper (ProseMirror's draggable leaf root) is the drag source and the picture node is dragged as the case is; or exclude `dragstart` from `stopEvent`. Keep `copy` stopped: PM's copy handler would serialize its own (stale) selection instead of the words the user selected.

Hardening, no exploit path: `DOMSerializer.renderSpec(document, toDOM(node))` omits the `blockArraysIn` argument prosemirror-view passes as `node.attrs` (index.js:1314), the guard that makes prosemirror-model throw on an array-valued attribute used as a DOM spec. Not reachable today (Milkdown's image attrs validate as strings). `renderSpec(document, toDOM(node), null, node.attrs)` matches the library.
